nodes.summary: `H` is closed under addition.
nodes.title: Sums of random variables

nodes.summary: Every constant function belongs to `H`.
nodes.title: Constants are random variables

nodes.summary: If `E` is a sublinear expectation on `H`, then for every `X ∈ H` there is a linear functional `f` on `H` with `f ≤ E` and `f X = E X`, and every such dominated linear functional is a *linear expectation*: monotone and constant preserving (Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Theorem 2.1). The linear expectations obtained this way are in general only finitely additive (Remark 2.2 there).
nodes.title: Representation of a sublinear expectation, pointwise form

nodes.summary: Let `E` be a subadditive and positively homogeneous functional on a real vector space. For every `x` there is a linear functional `f ≤ E` with `f x = E x` (S. Peng, *Nonlinear Expectations and Stochastic Calculus under Uncertainty*, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Theorem 2.1, first part; the proof is the Hahn–Banach extension of `c • x ↦ c * E x` from the line through `x`).
nodes.title: Representation of a sublinear functional, pointwise form

nodes.summary: Cash translatability (S. Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Remark 1.4 (vi)): `E[c + X] = c + E[X]`.
nodes.title: Cash translatability

nodes.summary: A G-normal random variable has zero upper mean (S. Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter II, Remark 1.5): if `X` is G-normally distributed then `E[X] = 0`. The proof compares `E[X + X̄] = 2 E[X]` (independence and identical distribution of the copy) with `E[X + X̄] = E[√2 X] = √2 E[X]` (the defining scaling with `a = b = 1`).
nodes.title: A G-normal random variable has zero upper mean

nodes.summary: A G-normal random variable has zero lower mean (S. Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter II, Remark 1.5): if `X` is G-normally distributed then `E[-X] = 0`, so `X` has no mean uncertainty.
nodes.title: A G-normal random variable has zero lower mean

nodes.summary: Identically distributed random vectors (S. Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Definition 3.1). `X₁` on `S₁` and `X₂` on `S₂`, with values in a normed group `F`, are identically distributed if `E₁[φ(X₁)] = E₂[φ(X₂)]` for every `φ ∈ C_{l.Lip}(F)`.
nodes.title: Identically distributed random vectors

nodes.summary: Independence under a sublinear expectation (S. Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Definition 3.10). `Y` is independent from `X` if `E[φ(X, Y)] = E[E[φ(x, Y)]_{x = X}]` for every `φ ∈ C_{l.Lip}`. The relation is not symmetric in `X` and `Y` (Remark 3.12 there).
nodes.title: Independence under a sublinear expectation

nodes.summary: If `ρ` is a coherent risk measure on `H`, then `A_ρ = {X ∈ H : ρ(X) ≤ 0}` is a coherent acceptable set (Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Exercise 5.6).
nodes.title: The acceptance set of a coherent risk measure

nodes.summary: Coherent acceptable set (Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Definition 5.1). A set `A` of positions in `H` is a coherent acceptable set if it is upward closed in `H`, contains `0` but not `-1`, and is closed under multiplication by nonnegative scalars and under convex combinations.
nodes.title: Coherent acceptable set

nodes.summary: If `E` is a sublinear expectation on `H`, then `ρ(X) = E[-X]` is a coherent risk measure (Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, §5, the remark following Proposition 5.5).
nodes.title: Sublinear expectations give coherent risk measures

nodes.summary: Coherent risk measure (after Artzner, Delbaen, Eber and Heath, 1999). A functional `ρ` on the space `H` of risk positions (containing the constants) is a coherent risk measure if it is antitone, satisfies `ρ(1) = -ρ(-1) = -1`, and is subadditive and positively homogeneous on `H`. These are the four properties that Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Proposition 5.5 proves for the risk measure…
nodes.title: Coherent risk measure

nodes.summary: G-normal distribution, one-dimensional (S. Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter II, Definition 1.4 with `d = 1`). A real random variable `X ∈ H` is (centred) G-normally distributed if it has an independent copy `X̄ ∈ H` (`X̄ =ᵈ X` and `X̄` independent from `X`) such that `aX + bX̄ =ᵈ √(a² + b²) X` for all `a, b ≥ 0`. Its law is determined by `σ̄² = E[X²]` and `σ²_ = -E[-X²]` (Chapter II, Proposition 1.7 for existence;…
nodes.title: G-normal distribution, one-dimensional

nodes.summary: If `Ω` is finite and `E` is a sublinear expectation on all functions `Ω → ℝ`, then `E[X] = max {∑_ω q(ω) X(ω) : q ∈ Q}`, where `Q` is the set of probability vectors `q` with `∑_ω q(ω) Y(ω) ≤ E[Y]` for every `Y`; the maximum is attained. This is the finite-`Ω` case of Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Theorem 2.1, which the Notes to Chapter I attribute to Huber (*Robust Statistics*, 1981).
nodes.title: Representation on a finite scenario set

nodes.summary: A subadditive and positively homogeneous functional `E` on a real vector space satisfies `E x = max {f x : f linear, f ≤ E}` for every `x`, the maximum being attained (Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Theorem 2.1, first part).
nodes.title: Representation of a sublinear functional as a maximum of linear functionals

nodes.summary: For a sublinear expectation `E` on `H` and `X ∈ H`, `E[X]` is the largest value of `f X` over the linear expectations `f` on `H` (monotone, constant preserving) dominated by `E`, and the maximum is attained: `E[X] = max_θ E_θ[X]` (Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Theorem 2.1).
nodes.title: Representation of a sublinear expectation as a maximum of linear expectations

nodes.summary: A constant function is in `C_{l.Lip}`.
nodes.title: Constants are test functions

nodes.summary: A Lipschitz function is in `C_{l.Lip}` (with `m = 0`).
nodes.title: Lipschitz functions are test functions

nodes.summary: Peng's test-function class `C_{l.Lip}` (S. Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, §1): `φ` satisfies `|φ(x) - φ(y)| ≤ C (1 + ‖x‖ᵐ + ‖y‖ᵐ) ‖x - y‖` for some `C` and some `m ∈ ℕ`. The class does not depend on the choice of an equivalent norm.
nodes.title: Peng's test-function class `C_{l.Lip}`

nodes.summary: If `ρ` is a coherent risk measure on `H`, then `E[X] = ρ(-X)` is a sublinear expectation (Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, §5, the remark following Proposition 5.5).
nodes.title: Coherent risk measures give sublinear expectations

nodes.summary: Sublinear expectation (Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Definition 1.1). `E` is a sublinear expectation on the linear space `H` of real functions on `Ω` if `H` contains the constants and `E` is monotone, constant preserving, subadditive and positively homogeneous on `H`. The functional is total on `Ω → ℝ`, but only its values on `H` are constrained. (Peng also assumes `|X| ∈ H` for `X ∈ H`; the results of this…
nodes.title: Sublinear expectation

nodes.summary: A coherent risk measure satisfies `ρ(c) = -c` for every constant `c`, from `ρ(1) = -ρ(-1) = -1` and positive homogeneity.
nodes.title: Coherent risk measures of constants

nodes.summary: If `E (c • x) = c * E x` for all `c > 0`, then `E 0 = 0`.
nodes.title: Positively homogeneous functionals vanish at zero

nodes.summary: Sublinear expectation space (S. Peng, arXiv:1002.4546v1, Chapter I, Definition 1.1 with the standing convention of §1). `H` is a set of real functions on `Ω`, closed under `(X₁, …, Xₙ) ↦ φ(X₁, …, Xₙ)` for `φ ∈ C_{l.Lip}(ℝⁿ)` (so it is a linear space containing the constants and `|X|` for each of its elements), and `E` is monotone, constant preserving, subadditive and positively homogeneous on `H`. `E` is total on…
nodes.title: Sublinear expectation space

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
